Government & public programmes

Structure maps and land evidence for public programmes

Structure layers and estimated households for planning, dated records of what has changed on public land, and before-and-after checks after floods and cyclones. Built for land, planning and service delivery, reviewed by a person and delivered as files your GIS team can use.

Tell us about your programme area How the method works

The problem, in your words

Planning needs to know what is on the ground now

Municipal land teams, settlement-upgrading programmes, disaster-recovery units and energy-access programmes all start from the same question: how many buildings are there, where, and how is that changing? Official maps are often years old in fast-growing places, and field enumeration is slow and costly to repeat.

“Our base map is years out of date.”

Settlements have grown since the last aerial survey. Planners need a current structure layer to load into their own GIS.

“Which areas flood, and what was damaged?”

Recovery teams need to know which structures sit in ground that floods, and what visibly changed after the event.

“How many households does each village have?”

Energy-access and service programmes need honest estimates, with the assumptions stated, before the field teams go out.

Who this is for

  • Municipal land-management, human-settlements and GIS departments
  • Settlement-upgrading programme managers
  • Disaster agencies and recovery programme units
  • Infrastructure owners’ risk managers
  • Energy-access programme units
  • Health programme GIS teams

Municipal land and settlement planning

A current structure layer, and what changed since

We deliver a GIS layer of structures across a district, municipality or imagery survey, ready for your own mapping system, with reviewer-led mapping where automatic detection is not enough, such as dense informal settlement or mixed tree cover. Structures inside and around public land parcels can be listed with their distance to the boundary.

Between dated surveys, new and removed structures are flagged and confirmed by a reviewer, and the area can be re-surveyed on a schedule agreed with you. A trend of built-up land over the years shows where settlement is growing fastest, estimated households support service planning, and a land-cover baseline adds built-up land, cropland, bare ground, water and tree cover. If your department holds its own aerial imagery, we work from that.

What you receive

  • A structure layer across the area, ready for your GIS
  • Structures inside and around public land parcels
  • New and removed structures between dated surveys
  • Settlement growth trends
  • Estimated households, with an assumptions table
  • A land-use and land-cover baseline

Disaster risk and recovery

Before the season, and after the event

Before the rainy or cyclone season, flood-exposure screening highlights the structures, roads and sites in ground seen as water in past satellite records, in low-lying areas or at river crossings, and terrain screening flags steep and erosion-prone ground. A structure layer and estimated households for the exposed areas support preparedness planning.

After a flood or cyclone, radar imagery maps the flooded area even under cloud, and a reviewer checks structures and assets before and after the event on optical or drone imagery captured once the weather allows.

Screening and checks, not modelling

Flood-exposure screening is not a hydraulic model, an official flood line or an insurance rating. Post-event work depends on imagery captured after the event, covers visible damage only, and is not an emergency or early-warning service.

Terrain, flood & post-event mapping

Steep, erosion-prone and flood-exposed stretches highlighted, and before-and-after checks along your route after storms and floods.

Energy-access programmes

Household estimates for electrification planning

Electrification programmes and the developers they fund need structure layers and estimated households across candidate communities, growth trends that show which villages are expanding, and land-cover context for generation sites. We deliver all four as layers and tables, with the assumptions behind every household figure set out in the report. The same work for developers is described under mini-grid and electrification planning.

Settlement & household estimates

Structure layers and estimated households for mini-grid sizing, service planning and consultation planning, with the assumptions stated.

Read

Public land and estates

Industrial estates, free zones and land banks

Public land, estates and free zones

For industrial estates, special economic zones, free zones, ports and public land banks, we list the structures inside the boundary and in a ring around it, flag change at the perimeter between dated surveys, with fence lines checked by a reviewer on drone imagery, and document the land’s history from archived imagery. It is a land record for planning and management, not a title or valuation check.

Health campaign microplanning

Structure layers and estimated households help health programmes plan campaigns, teams and supplies for each settlement. We combine our reviewed structure layer with open population data, such as WorldPop and, in Nigeria, GRID3, credited as their terms require, and state the assumptions. It is not a census, and a structure’s category describes what the imagery shows, not what the building is used for.

Encroachment surveys

Structures inside a concession, site or boundary, in a ring around it, or both, mapped and listed so you can see where land is being occupied.

Mozambique, South Africa, Nigeria

Public programmes in each country

A summary for orientation, as of 26 September 2026, not legal advice.

Português · English

Mozambique

The cyclone season, roughly November to April, makes pre-season exposure screening and post-event checks the most useful work for the national disaster institute (INGD), municipal councils and urban programmes. Protection zones under the Land Law (art. 8) are public domain, so structure layers along roads, railways and conduits help public land custodians. Reports can be delivered in Portuguese.

English

South Africa

Municipalities procure under the Municipal Finance Management Act, and settlement-upgrading programmes, including those supported by the Housing Development Agency, need current structure layers and household estimates. If a register is to be used as evidence about unlawful conduct, POPIA’s prior-authorisation rule (s57) may apply to your organisation, so take advice first: our work for municipalities is scoped for planning and service delivery.

English

Nigeria

The Rural Electrification Agency runs energy-access programmes, including the World Bank-financed DARES, and the National Emergency Management Agency leads on disasters. GRID3 Nigeria already publishes open settlement data; what we add is a reviewed structure layer for your area, change between dates and stated assumptions.

Honest scope

What we do, and what we don’t

What we do

  • Map structures and land cover for planning and service delivery
  • Estimate households from structure counts, with the assumptions stated
  • Screen flood exposure and check visible damage after events
  • Flag change between dated surveys, confirmed by a reviewer

What we don’t do

  • Take a census or enumerate households
  • Decide whether a structure is lawful, or support evictions or enforcement
  • Run an emergency, early-warning or public-safety service
  • Verify title, tenure or building use

Frequently asked questions

Is a household estimate a census?

No. Households are estimated from structure counts using stated persons-per-household assumptions drawn from national census data, and every report sets the assumptions out. It is a planning figure, not a count of people.

Can your maps be used for enforcement or evictions?

We map land for planning and service delivery. We do not decide whether a structure is lawful, and our work is not designed for enforcement or evictions; decisions about occupation rest with the authorities and the courts.

Can you map damage straight after a cyclone?

Post-event mapping depends on imagery captured after the event. Radar can map the flooded area even under cloud; checks of visible damage need optical or drone imagery captured once the weather allows. It is not an emergency or early-warning service.

Can we use our own aerial imagery?

Yes. If your department already holds orthophotos or satellite scenes, we run the same structure and change analysis on them. Results depend on the imagery’s quality and resolution.

Tell us about your programme area

A district, a settlement list or a programme boundary is enough to scope a structure layer, household estimates or a change survey.
